title: How Marc Lou ships 35 startups solo: deep work, a 5% hit rate and constant launching
summary: Marc Lou walks through his daily routine as a solo founder making $77K/month. He protects a 4 to 6 hour offline coding block, ships constantly because only about 5% of his 35 startups worked, and keeps his AI setup simple. The core idea is that launch volume, not polish or productivity tooling, is what eventually produces a winner.

principles.text: Ship many products; a hit is a numbers game with roughly a 5% hit rate.
principles.quote: I shipped about 35 startups and on those 35, 30 of them are nothing. They don't work. They barely don't make any money. They barely don't have any users. So, the heater rate is about 5%.

principles.text: Keep rolling the dice: repeated launches eventually produce a winner you can build on.
principles.quote: if you keep playing, you keep playing, playing, playing, and playing, at some point one dice one roll of dice will work.

principles.text: Protect a long offline deep work block each morning and do only creation in it.
principles.quote: I just want to have this big block of time that is usually 4 to 6 hours where I really deep work.

principles.text: Keep support, email and social for later in the day so they cannot hijack your best hours.
principles.quote: If that happens at the beginning of the day, then I'll fix this bug instead of actually working on what truly matters for me, which is creating more stuff.

principles.text: Validate an idea by shipping it with a buy button, not by thinking about it.
principles.quote: The only way to validate an idea is to ship it with a buy button.

principles.text: In the AI era the KPI is still the number of things you ship; keep the setup simple.
principles.quote: I think the the single KPI that matters hasn't changed in the AI era. It's still the number of things you ship.
